A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CraftMesh and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references supporting a reliable comparison. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original mesh-editing comparisons, CLIP measurements in Table 1, drag-editing demonstrations, and qualitative component ablations.

after.justification: V2 reports original comparative measurements in Table 1, quantitative ablations in Table 2, and qualitative editing and loss-ablation results.

M1.justification: V1's mesh parameterization, Delaunay densification, and linear Poisson color solve are replaced by neural color-field optimization with distribution, gradient, and boundary losses in v2 Section 3.2.2. Region generation also changes from separate CraftsMan3D generations to extracting parts from a MeshyAI reference mesh, with separate region generation optional. The geometric normal-blending core remains.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate detailed 3D objects through insertion, deletion/replacement, and drag-based editing. The additional cat demonstration and revised sculpture appearance remain within this coverage. V2's six-object count newly documents dataset size rather than establishing a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: The comparative evaluation retains FocalDreamer, MagicClay, and Instant3dit. Boolean fusion already provides the unrefined geometry reference in v1; v2 expands component-ablation comparisons without introducing another competing mesh-editing method.

E3.justification: V2 adds NIQE and NIMA to the two CLIP metrics and introduces a quantitative four-configuration ablation design: Boolean baseline, geometry only, texture only, and full method. The evaluated mesh generator changes from CraftsMan3D to MeshyAI. Geometry optimization remains 1000 iterations on a 4090 GPU; the newly disclosed object count does not establish a sample-size change.

E4.justification: V1 tests geometry fusion and texture harmonization qualitatively. V2 adds quantitative component isolation in Table 2 and separate distribution-, gradient-, and boundary-loss removals in Figure 6, testing their effects on color harmony, detail, and seams. Figure 5 also adds a cat-paw drag-editing case.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. V2's additional tables retain single-value reporting.

E6.justification: All Table 1 CLIP scores change: CraftMesh's CLIPsim/CLIPdir values are 11.866/25.488 in v1 and 22.768/13.594 in v2. V2 additionally reports NIQE 3.203 and NIMA 5.071, quantitative ablation results, and expanded qualitative comparisons. These are revised-configuration results, not controlled evidence of improvement or deterioration between versions.

T1.justification: V1's discrete gradient/Laplacian formulation and linear color solve are replaced by a kernel-density color definition and distribution, gradient-preservation, and distance-weighted boundary objectives in v2 Equations 7–12. Geometry Equations 1–6 remain substantively unchanged. The change concerns mathematical formulation; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central pipeline, high-fidelity editing objective, and superiority claims remain. V2 strengthens novelty to the 'first' image-editing–mesh-generation–fusion framework and recasts the separate fusion contributions as joint geometry and appearance optimization in implicit and explicit representations.

C2.justification: V2 explains the distinct roles of color-distribution alignment, gradient preservation, and boundary consistency, supported by new ablations. Its conclusion adds concrete limitations involving open, multilayer, or noisy meshes and dependence on pretrained generators; v1 only suggests future robustness work generically.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the neural color-field backbone, discloses six evaluation objects, and reports texture optimization as 2000 iterations taking one minute on a 4090 GPU. It also promises implementation release upon acceptance, without providing released code. These improve documentation but do not establish additional runs or a larger dataset.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for CLIP, NIQE, and NIMA, replaces Qwen3 with Qwen-Image, and removes the standalone 3DGS and Hunyuan3D 2.0 references. It sharpens the contrast with classical Poisson mesh editing regarding smoothing and detail preservation, while retaining the principal related-work categories and competing approaches.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively condensed and rewritten. Geometry and texture sections are reorganized under joint fusion, quantitative results precede qualitative results, and terminology changes from Poisson Geometric Fusion to Poisson Geometry Blending. Authorship and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout with substantial figure redesign. The overview incorporates the new texture losses, qualitative comparisons expand from four to six rows with geometry renderings for each method, and drag/ablation panels are reorganized. Table 1 is transposed and expanded, and Table 2 is added.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens v1's qualitative component validation with quantitative controls, individual texture-loss ablations, perceptual metrics, and concrete limitations. These provide a limited net improvement in evidence and transparency. However, changed generators prevent attributing the revised scores to fusion alone, and Equation 11 leaves cutoff and zero-distance handling unspecified; its weight does not globally decay with distance as claimed.
